questions: Section 10 refers a hazardous occupation appearing together with a hazardous avocation to underwriting judgement. On this file (class C high-voltage lineman who also does technical trad rock climbing, 13 days a year), does the desk simply add the two 50-debit charges, or does it handle the combination differently - for example an exclusion rider on the climbing in place of its debits?

Section 12 has a single band, 'elevated liver enzymes: 25'. This applicant's enzymes are above twice the upper limit of normal with no alcohol history. Is an elevation over 2x ULN rated at that same 25, charged more heavily than 25, or postponed pending further investigation?

Section 16 refers combinations of cardiac risk factors to underwriting judgement. In a 54-year-old male, does BMI 28.3 together with HDL 39 and A1c 5.8 count as such a combination, and if so what does the desk do with it?
